data.title: Thursday Analyst Calls: Anthropic Initiated, Nvidia Target Cut, Apple and SpaceX Ratings Reiterated, Box and Abbott Upgraded, Strategy Downgraded
data.description: According to CNBC, Wolfe initiated coverage of Anthropic with an outperform rating, while JPMorgan reiterated its overweight rating on Apple, citing survey results that showed iPhone purchase intent at its highest level in five years. Morgan Stanley reiterated SpaceX at overweight. UBS upgraded Box to buy from neutral, citing accelerating AI-driven growth, and Leerink upgraded Abbott Labs to outperform from market perform. Daiwa maintained its outperform rating on Nvidia but cut its price target to $185 per share from $245. Monness Crespi Hardt downgraded Strategy to sell from neutral, citing BTC exposure, leverage and the stock’s premium to its BTC holdings.

data.title: Soitec Raises Guidance as Shares Jump More Than 15% on AI Demand
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Soitec raised its guidance for the full fiscal year ending in March 2027, citing strong artificial intelligence demand and customer cash deposits to secure products for AI infrastructure. The company expects revenue to grow about 40% year over year, assuming constant currency and business scope, and said demand provides enough visibility to issue full-year guidance rather than its usual quarterly forecasts.

Analyst Pavan Daswani wrote that the guidance implied fiscal 2027 revenue of about €830 million, above the €750 million consensus estimate. He said Soitec had received about $1.2 billion in customer cash deposits for purchases over the next several years, indicating demand exceeds supply. Soitec is also discussing additional orders for fiscal 2028 and expanding capacity.

Shares rose more than 15% in early Paris trading on Thursday. The stock had gained more than threefold since the start of the year, while its market capitalization had increased more than fourfold. The company said fiscal 2027 revenue from its Photonics-SOI product would exceed $300 million, more than double the year-earlier level and above its previous guidance range of $250 million to $300 million, raised in September. Sales in the second quarter, ended September 30, rose to €204 million from €139 million a year earlier. Edge and cloud AI was the largest revenue source, contributing €107 million, more than double the year-earlier amount.

data.title: MapleStory Universe Suspends Services for Emergency Maintenance, Says Player Assets Are Safe
data.description:
MapleStory Universe said it suspended services multiple times for emergency maintenance and that player assets remain safe. According to Foresight News, the blockchain game detected another attack attempt on November 18 after facing repeated attempts recently; the team said its security checks found that the attacks had been blocked.

The team reported no damage to player assets, on-chain contracts, game records, or sensitive information, and said a broader investigation is ongoing. It is assessing the impact on players whose game challenges were interrupted or who did not claim weekly rewards, and is preparing targeted compensation. Details will be announced later.

data.title: Trump, Xi and Putin Promise More Fuel, but Oil Markets Barely Move
data.description:
Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin pledged to increase global supplies of refined petroleum products, but oil prices barely moved Thursday. Their joint declaration called for more diesel and gasoline but set no production targets, delivery dates or distribution details, according to BeInCrypto. The leaders made the announcement at a meeting in Shenzhen, China, on November 19. Brent crude rose 0.18%, while US crude gained 0.15%.

Trump announced a diesel supply deal with Putin on October 9, but US diesel still costs around $5.96 per gallon, down 32 cents since the announcement and roughly 58% higher than a year ago, according to AAA. The Federal Reserve’s latest minutes cited persistent inflation concerns, and markets priced in a 92% probability of a quarter-point rate hike in December. Higher rates are weighing on risk assets, including Bitcoin, while a stronger dollar is pressuring gold.

data.title: Bill Zerella Joins Stord to Accelerate Expansion Through Organic Growth and Acquisitions
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, veteran CFO Bill Zerella joined logistics startup Stord in August to accelerate its expansion and improve operating margins through organic growth and acquisitions. Stord operates more than 100 warehouses and fulfillment centers and provides warehousing and fulfillment services to brands. The 11-year-old company completed a $250 million Series F round earlier this year at a $3 billion post-money valuation and added a $400 million credit facility.

Last month, Stord acquired third-party logistics provider AMS Fulfillment, its 12th acquisition and largest to date. Zerella said the credit facility is for acquisitions, while Series F equity funding will support other business operations and growth. He said Stord remains interested in acquisitions that strengthen its network; the United States has about 14,000 third-party logistics companies.

Zerella has nearly 30 years of CFO experience and has helped three venture-backed companies go public: Vocera Communications in 2012, Fitbit in 2015 and ACV Auctions in 2021. Stryker acquired Vocera in 2022, and Google acquired Fitbit in 2021.

In an interview with CFO Journal, Zerella said Stord's priority is scaling the business. He said the company has a clear path to positive EBITDA but gave no timeline. Funding needs beyond organic growth will depend on the pace of acquisitions.

data.title: Pine Labs Launches Staq Web3 Orchestrator for Stablecoin-Linked Card Programs
data.description: Pine Labs, an Indian payments and commercial infrastructure company, has launched Staq Web3 Orchestrator, a platform for businesses to introduce stablecoin-linked card programs through existing payment networks. According to Foresight News, the platform integrates card issuance, wallets, custody, compliance, liquidity and currency exchange services through partners. Hong Kong-based Reap provides card issuance support and access to the Visa network for stablecoin-linked cards on the platform.

data.title: Kaspersky: Retadup Spreads Through Old USB Devices Seven Years After Server Seizure
data.description:
Retadup, a botnet previously used to distribute cryptocurrency-mining malware, has become active again, spreading through previously infected USB storage devices and delivering the CoffeeLoader malware loader to affected devices. According to Foresight News, cybersecurity firm Kaspersky said it blocked about 15,000 related attack attempts in Peru, Angola, Bolivia, Russia, and other countries during the first nine months of 2026.

The botnet’s command-and-control server was taken over by law enforcement in 2019, but malware may remain on some offline devices and USB drives. The latest activity could lead to information theft or ransomware infections, rather than being limited to illicit cryptocurrency mining.

data.title: Nike Taps GTA 6 Hype With Travis Scott Sneaker Drop as Stock Sheds Over 40%
data.description:
Nike is using a Travis Scott sneaker collaboration tied to GTA 6 to build excitement as it tries to persuade Wall Street its turnaround can work; its stock has lost more than 40% this year. The black-and-white Travis Scott x Rockstar x Nike Air Force 1 Low is priced at $130 per pair, according to BeInCrypto, with releases listed through London’s Selfridges, Nike’s SNKRS app and Scott’s Cactus Jack store. The shoes feature GTA lettering, and the black pair has a debossed game map. A friends-and-family edition will not be sold publicly, while the white pair is listed on StockX for several times its retail price ahead of the official drop. Scott also appears on the game’s soundtrack and is set to join Rockstar’s Miami launch festival. Strategy released $250 Bitcoin Jordans earlier this year, but buyers could not pay with crypto.

Nike’s Full Stride Ahead plan targets about $5 billion in additional revenue by fiscal 2031, focusing on five sports and 23 priority countries. The company expects sales to keep falling before growth returns in fiscal 2029, and its stock closed 6.3% lower on the day of its investor-day presentation. Quarterly earnings in December are the next test. Sensor Tower estimates GTA 6 sold about 17 million copies for more than $1.65 billion by launch; some analysts expect more than $3 billion in first-week sales. The game’s hype has also helped leave the PS5 Pro sold out at major U.S. retailers, while near-perfect reviews lifted Take-Two stock.

data.title: Strike Risk Intensifies at Los Angeles and Long Beach Ports
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, the Pacific Maritime Association said Wednesday that the West Coast’s busiest container port complex faces a strike threat as the current labor contract approaches its expiration at 12:01 a.m. Saturday. The association said it was still struggling to reach an agreement with the local union representing 250 security guards at the Port of Los Angeles and the Port of Long Beach.

The International Longshore and Warehouse Union, which represents the guards, declined to comment. The unarmed guards have completed a strike vote and work at six container terminals that handle more than half of the containers at the Los Angeles-Long Beach port complex. Although the guards account for just 2% of the union’s total workforce at the ports, employers said other unionized dockworkers would refuse to cross picket lines.

The employers’ group said the union’s demands had not materially changed since negotiations began more than a year ago. The union has extended the current contract twice and is unwilling to extend it again. The parties are scheduled to resume negotiations Friday.

data.title: Lynx Equity: Micron Valuation Is “Incredibly” Low; Anthropic Listing May Revive AI Investment
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Lynx Equity analyst KC Rajkumar said on November 19 that fears of slowing investment in AI infrastructure are more than reflected in semiconductor stock valuations. Slower approvals for data center construction do not signal weaker chip demand, and recent pullbacks in memory chip and semiconductor equipment stocks have created attractive buying opportunities. Micron Technology is his top pick, with a price target of $1,325.

Rajkumar said investors are misreading delays in data center construction approvals as a structural slowdown in AI infrastructure spending. He sees little evidence that the delays have altered demand prospects over the next several years for DRAM, NAND flash, CPUs or semiconductor equipment. He expects upcoming industry investor conferences to reinforce previous demand forecasts and restore confidence in the AI infrastructure investment cycle.

Rajkumar said Anthropic’s listing today could be a catalyst for a rebound in AI-related stocks. A successful IPO could revive investment enthusiasm for the AI sector, while a higher listing valuation could strengthen Anthropic’s financing capacity to support its AI infrastructure investment commitments. Seven technology companies have subscribed to a combined $26 billion in shares through private placements tied to IPO pricing. Rajkumar expects those investors and other industry participants to continue supporting the company after its listing.

He said Micron’s valuation is “incredibly” low, at about 2.3 times earnings based on his 2028 earnings-per-share forecast, and expects the stock could rebound as investors reassess the durability of memory chip demand. His price targets are $2,450 for SanDisk and $400 for Lam Research. Rajkumar has also become more optimistic about AMD and Intel, saying demand for high-core-count CPU servers should remain resilient even if spending centered on Nvidia GPUs cools. He said semiconductor stocks have considerable room to rebound if long-term industry demand expectations remain stable and Anthropic’s listing restores confidence in AI investment.

data.title: STOCKS | Barclays Names European Medical Technology Top Picks, Favors EssilorLuxottica, Philips and Fresenius
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Barclays published a research report on Europe’s medical technology and services sector on November 19, naming EssilorLuxottica its top pick and favoring companies with strong competitive barriers, stable demand and clear earnings growth prospects.

Barclays said expectations for growth in EssilorLuxottica’s wearables business had been substantially lowered and were now more reasonable. It said the company’s core eyewear business has strong competitive barriers and resilient demand, and that its shares trade at a significant discount to the bank’s assessment of fair value.

Among medical-device makers, Barclays favored Philips, with its adjusted EBIT forecast 6% above market consensus. The bank said it had become more confident in management’s ability to deliver earnings growth and viewed Philips’ patient-monitoring business as differentiated. It said the sector faces potential tariff increases, rising production costs and limited pricing power, but demand is resilient and reimbursement-policy and regulatory risks are relatively low.

Barclays preferred Fresenius Group over its former controlled subsidiary Fresenius Medical Care, forecasting stable mid-single-digit growth. It said expansion at Fresenius Kabi could push the group’s medium-term margin above its target. A recent strategic biosimilar deal could generate an additional €2.5 billion in revenue, a long-term growth opportunity Barclays said was not fully reflected in the valuation. Fresenius traded at about 14 times estimated 2027 earnings, compared with 22 times for Sandoz; Barclays expected the valuation gap to narrow gradually.
